source.text: כִּ֛י נַ֥עַר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וָאֹהֲבֵ֑הוּ וּמִמִּצְרַ֖יִם קָרָ֥אתִי לִבְנִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: When [was] a youth Israel, and I loved him, and out of Egypt I called to my son.

en.L: When Israel [was] a boy, I loved him, \q and out of Egypt I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son.
en.B: When Israel was a boy, I loved him, \q and out of Egypt I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son.
en.R: When Israel was a child, I loved him. \q I called {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son out of Egypt.

es.L: Cuando Israel [era] muchacho, yo lo amé, \q y de Egipto llamé a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo.
es.B: Cuando Israel era un muchacho, yo lo amé, \q y de Egipto llamé a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo.
es.R: Cuando Israel era niño, yo lo amé. \q Llamé a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo a salir de Egipto.

fr.L: Quand Israël [était] un garçon, je l’ai aimé, \q et d’Égypte j’ai appelé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils.
fr.B: Quand Israël était un garçon, je l’ai aimé, \q et d’Égypte j’ai appelé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils.
fr.R: Quand Israël était un enfant, je l’ai aimé. \q J’ai appelé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils à sortir d’Égypte.

sw.L: Israeli alipokuwa kijana, nilimpenda, \q na kutoka Misri nilimwita mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}.
sw.B: Israeli alipokuwa kijana, nilimpenda, \q na nilimwita mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kutoka Misri.
sw.R: Israeli alipokuwa mtoto, nilimpenda. \q Nilimwita mwana {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} atoke Misri.

vi.L: Khi Y-sơ-ra-ên [còn] là một cậu bé, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu nó, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gọi con {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra khỏi Ai Cập.
vi.B: Khi Y-sơ-ra-ên còn là một cậu bé, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu thương nó, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã gọi con {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra khỏi Ai Cập.
vi.R: Khi Y-sơ-ra-ên còn thơ ấu, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã yêu thương nó. \q Ta đã gọi con {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ra khỏi Ai Cập.

ko.L: 이스라엘이 어린아이였을 때에 내가 그를 사랑했고, \q 내가 이집트에서 내 아들을 불러내었다.
ko.B: 이스라엘이 어린아이였을 때에 나는 그를 사랑했다. \q 그리고 내가 내 아들을 이집트에서 불러내었다.
ko.R: 이스라엘이 어린아이였을 때에 나는 그를 사랑했다. \q 나는 내 아들을 이집트에서 불러냈다.

decisions.choice: out of Egypt I called my son: the exodus, quoted in Matthew 2:15
alternatives: a prediction about the Messiah only
decisions.reason: The son is Israel, the people God brought out of Egypt; God had told Pharaoh, "Israel is my son, my firstborn" (Exodus 4:22-23). Hosea looks back on the exodus as the start of a father's love. Matthew 2:15 quotes these words of Jesus, God's Son, who went down into Egypt and came out again, living through Israel's story himself. Matthew's words agree with the Hebrew here ("my son"); the Greek translation of Hosea reads "his children", so Matthew did not take the line from it. This description of the Greek is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: a boy, a child: Israel's earliest days as a people, in Egypt and at the exodus
decisions.reason: The word covers a boy from infancy to youth. Hosea pictures the nation's beginnings as a childhood, as he speaks of "the days of her youth" when Israel came up from Egypt (2:17). Verses 3-4 go on with the picture: a parent teaching a small child to walk and stooping to feed it.

decisions.choice: I loved him: love that came first, before Israel had done anything
decisions.reason: God's love is the starting point of the chapter. It was not earned: the LORD set his love on Israel when they were a small and enslaved people (Deuteronomy 7:7-8). The rest of the chapter weighs this love against Israel's turning away (verses 2-7) and ends with love winning out (verses 8-11).

decisions.choice: I called my son out of Egypt: God summoned his son to leave Egypt
alternatives: ever since Egypt I have called my son (compare 12:10; 13:4, "from the land of Egypt")
decisions.reason: The verb "call" takes a small word "to" before "my son", as calling often does in Hebrew. Read with "out of Egypt", it is the summons of the exodus. Verse 2 picks up the same verb: God called, and others called, but Israel went the other way.

decisions.choice: Out of Egypt I called my son (L, B); I called my son out of Egypt (R)
alternatives: Out of Egypt I called to my son
decisions.reason: Each level uses the same words for this line as Open Word Bible's Matthew 2:15 at that level, so a reader can see the quotation (m1). Literal does not show the small word "to", since English "call" needs no word before its object; the meaning is the same.

decisions.choice: my son (deity pronoun setting on "my")
decisions.reason: God is speaking, so "my" takes the deity pronoun setting, as it does in Matthew 2:15. "Him" and "son" refer to Israel and take no setting.

decisions.choice: "de Egipto llamé a mi hijo" (L, B); "Llamé a mi hijo a salir de Egipto" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:15 quotes this line, and the Hebrew and the Greek agree, so each level uses the wording of the Spanish Matthew at the same level, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "d'Égypte j'ai appelé mon fils" (L, B), "J'ai appelé mon fils à sortir d'Égypte" (R), the words of the published Matthew 2:15 at each level
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:15 quotes this line and agrees with the Hebrew, so each level keeps the French of Matthew, and "mon" takes the deity pronoun setting as there.

decisions.choice: "kutoka Misri nilimwita mwana wangu" (L), "nilimwita mwana wangu kutoka Misri" (B), "Nilimwita mwana wangu atoke Misri" (R), as the published Matthew 2:15
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:15 quotes this line and agrees with the Hebrew, so each level keeps the Swahili of Matthew; "wangu" takes the deity pronoun setting as there.

decisions.choice: "Ta đã gọi con Ta ra khỏi Ai Cập" at every level, as the published Matthew 2:15
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:15 quotes this line and agrees with the Hebrew, so every level keeps Matthew's Vietnamese wording.

decisions.choice: "내가 이집트에서 내 아들을 불러내었다" (L); "내가 내 아들을 이집트에서 불러내었다" (B); "…불러냈다" (R)
decisions.reason: Matthew 2:15 quotes this line, and here the Hebrew and the Greek agree, so each level uses the wording of the Korean Matthew 2:15 at that level.

source.text: קָרְא֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם כֵּ֚ן הָלְכ֣וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַבְּעָלִ֣ים יְזַבֵּ֔חוּ וְלַפְּסִלִ֖ים יְקַטֵּרֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: They called to them; so they went from before them; to the Baals they sacrificed, and to the carved images they made smoke.

en.L: They called to them; \q so they went away from them. \q To the Baals they sacrificed, \q and to the carved images they burned offerings.
en.B: The more they called to them, \q the more they went away from them. \q They sacrificed to the Baals \q and burned offerings to carved idols.
en.R: The more the prophets called to Israel, \q the more the people turned away. \q They offered sacrifices to the Baals \q and burned offerings to idols.

es.L: Los llamaban; \q así se iban de ellos. \q A los baales sacrificaban, \q y a las imágenes talladas quemaban ofrendas.
es.B: Cuanto más los llamaban, \q más se alejaban de ellos. \q Ofrecían sacrificios a los baales \q y quemaban ofrendas a los ídolos tallados.
es.R: Cuanto más llamaban los profetas a Israel, \q más se alejaba el pueblo. \q Ofrecían sacrificios a los baales \q y quemaban ofrendas a los ídolos.

fr.L: Ils les ont appelés ; \q ainsi ils s’en sont allés loin d’eux. \q Aux Baals ils ont sacrifié, \q et aux images taillées ils ont brûlé des offrandes.
fr.B: Plus on les appelait, \q plus ils s’éloignaient de ceux qui les appelaient. \q Ils offraient des sacrifices aux Baals \q et brûlaient des offrandes aux idoles taillées.
fr.R: Plus les prophètes appelaient Israël, \q plus le peuple se détournait. \q Ils offraient des sacrifices aux Baals \q et brûlaient des offrandes aux idoles.

sw.L: Waliwaita; \q hivyo wakaenda mbali nao. \q Kwa Mabaali walitoa dhabihu, \q na kwa sanamu za kuchonga walifukiza [sadaka].
sw.B: Kadiri walivyowaita, \q ndivyo walivyozidi kwenda mbali nao. \q Waliwatolea Mabaali dhabihu \q na kufukiza sadaka kwa sanamu za kuchonga.
sw.R: Kadiri manabii walivyowaita Israeli, \q ndivyo watu walivyozidi kugeuka mbali. \q Waliwatolea Mabaali dhabihu \q na kufukiza sadaka kwa sanamu.

vi.L: Họ đã gọi chúng; \q thế là chúng bỏ đi khỏi họ. \q Cho các thần Ba-anh chúng dâng sinh tế, \q và cho các tượng chạm chúng đốt của lễ.
vi.B: Họ càng gọi chúng, \q chúng càng bỏ đi xa họ. \q Chúng dâng sinh tế cho các thần Ba-anh \q và đốt của lễ cho các tượng chạm.
vi.R: Các nhà tiên tri càng kêu gọi Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q dân chúng càng quay đi. \q Chúng dâng sinh tế cho các thần Ba-anh \q và đốt của lễ cho các thần tượng.

ko.L: 그들이 그들을 불렀으나, \q 그들은 그들 앞에서 떠나갔다. \q 그들은 바알들에게 제사를 드리고, \q 새긴 우상들에게 분향했다.
ko.B: 부르면 부를수록 \q 그들은 더 멀리 떠나갔다. \q 그들은 바알들에게 제사를 드리고, \q 새긴 우상들에게 향을 피웠다.
ko.R: 예언자들이 이스라엘을 부르면 부를수록 \q 백성은 더 멀리 떠나갔다. \q 그들은 바알들에게 제물을 바치고, \q 우상들에게 향을 피웠다.

decisions.choice: They called to them ... away from them: messengers called Israel, and Israel walked away from them
alternatives: As I called them, so they went away from me (the reading of the Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "they called", most naturally the prophets and other messengers God sent (12:11; 2 Kings 17:13), and Israel went away from them. The Greek translation reads "as I called them, so they went away from me", which continues God's own calling from verse 1; the difference is a matter of a few letters. The Hebrew text is followed. This description of the Greek is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: so they went: the more they were called, the more they went away
decisions.reason: "So" sets the going away against the calling as its match: each call was answered by more distance.

decisions.choice: the Baals and carved images: the gods of Canaan and the idols that stood for them
decisions.reason: Baal was the Canaanite storm god, believed to give rain and harvest. "The Baals" are the local forms of his worship at many shrines (2:15, 19). Carved images were idols shaped from wood or stone, or cast and then shaped (8:4-6; 13:2).

decisions.choice: burned offerings: made sacrifices go up in smoke
decisions.reason: The verb means to make something go up in smoke. It is used for burning incense and for burning the parts of a sacrifice on the altar (4:13). Here it stands beside "sacrificed" for the whole of the worship given to idols.

decisions.choice: the prophets ... the people (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names who called and who turned away, so that the two "they"s are not confused. It follows the reading chosen in m1; the Hebrew itself does not name the callers.

decisions.choice: The more ... the more (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the more ... the more" to make plain how each call was matched by more distance (m2).

source.text: וְאָנֹכִ֤י תִרְגַּ֨לְתִּי֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם קָחָ֖ם עַל־זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כִּ֥י רְפָאתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And I, I taught to walk Ephraim, taking them by his arms; and not they knew that I healed them.

en.L: And I, I taught Ephraim to walk, \q taking them by his arms, \q but they did not know that I healed them.
en.B: Yet it was I who taught Ephraim to walk, \q holding them by the arms, \q but they did not know that I was the one who healed them.
en.R: I was the one who taught Ephraim to walk. \q I held them by the arms. \q But they did not know that I was the one who healed them.

es.L: Y yo, yo enseñé a andar a Efraín, \q tomándolos de sus brazos, \q pero no supieron que yo los sanaba.
es.B: Sin embargo, fui yo quien enseñó a andar a Efraín, \q sosteniéndolos por los brazos, \q pero no reconocieron que era yo quien los sanaba.
es.R: Fui yo quien le enseñó a caminar a Efraín. \q Yo los sostenía de los brazos. \q Pero no se dieron cuenta de que era yo quien los sanaba.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, j’ai appris à marcher à Éphraïm, \q les prenant par ses bras, \q mais ils n’ont pas su que je les guérissais.
fr.B: Pourtant, c’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui ai appris à marcher à Éphraïm, \q en les tenant par les bras, \q mais ils n’ont pas reconnu que c’était {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui les guérissais.
fr.R: C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui ai appris à Éphraïm à marcher. \q Je les tenais par les bras. \q Mais ils ne savaient pas que c’était {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui les guérissais.

sw.L: Na {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, nilimfundisha Efraimu kutembea, \q nikiwashika kwa mikono yake, \q lakini hawakujua kwamba niliwaponya.
sw.B: Hata hivyo, ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyemfundisha Efraimu kutembea, \q nikiwashika mikono, \q lakini hawakujua kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyewaponya.
sw.R: Ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyemfundisha Efraimu kutembea. \q Niliwashika mikono. \q Lakini hawakujua kwamba ni {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} niliyewaponya.

vi.L: Và chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã tập cho Ép-ra-im bước đi, \q nắm lấy chúng bởi cánh tay nó, \q nhưng chúng không biết rằng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã chữa lành chúng.
vi.B: Thế mà chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã tập cho Ép-ra-im bước đi, \q nắm lấy cánh tay chúng, \q nhưng chúng không biết rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đấng đã chữa lành chúng.
vi.R: Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã tập cho Ép-ra-im bước đi. \q Ta nắm lấy cánh tay chúng. \q Nhưng chúng không biết rằng chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đấng đã chữa lành chúng.

ko.L: 내가, 바로 내가 에브라임에게 걸음마를 가르쳤고, \q 그들의 팔을 붙잡아 주었다. \q 그러나 그들은 내가 그들을 고쳐 준 줄을 알지 못했다.
ko.B: 에브라임에게 걸음마를 가르친 것은 바로 나였다. \q 나는 그들의 팔을 붙잡아 주었다. \q 그러나 그들은 그들을 고쳐 준 이가 나라는 것을 알지 못했다.
ko.R: 에브라임에게 걷는 법을 가르쳐 준 것은 바로 나였다. \q 나는 그들의 팔을 붙잡아 주었다. \q 그러나 그들은 그들을 낫게 해 준 이가 나라는 것을 알지 못했다.

decisions.choice: I taught Ephraim to walk: the patient care of a parent for a toddler
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for "foot" and is found only here. The picture of verse 1 goes on: God is the parent guiding the child's first steps. The stressed "I" sets God's care against Israel's going after the Baals (verse 2).

decisions.choice: taking them by his arms: the Hebrew as written, the parent holding the child up by the arms
alternatives: I took them up in my arms (the reading of the ancient translations)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "taking them by his arms", that is, by Ephraim's arms, as a parent steadies a child learning to walk. The Greek, Syriac and Latin translations read "I took them up in my arms", which changes the person of two words. Both give the same picture of care. This description of the ancient translations is written from general knowledge.

decisions.choice: I healed them: the LORD as Israel's healer
decisions.reason: At the start of the wilderness journey the LORD said, "I am the LORD who heals you" (Exodus 15:26). Hosea often uses healing for God's restoring of his people (5:13; 6:1; 7:1; 14:5). Israel did not see whose care had kept them.

decisions.choice: Ephraim ... them: the people as one child and as many people
decisions.reason: Hosea moves between the singular (Ephraim, "him", "his") and the plural ("them") because Ephraim is both one son and a whole people.

decisions.choice: it was I who ... I was the one who (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew stresses "I" at the start and in "I healed them". Balanced and Readable carry the stress with "it was I who" and "I was the one who"; Literal repeats "I".

source.text: בְּחַבְלֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶמְשְׁכֵם֙ בַּעֲבֹת֣וֹת אַהֲבָ֔ה וָאֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם כִּמְרִ֥ימֵי עֹ֖ל עַ֣ל לְחֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו אוֹכִֽיל׃

records.literal_gloss: With cords of a human I drew them, with ropes of love; and I was to them like those who lift a yoke on their jaws, and I bent down to him; I fed [him].

en.L: With cords of a human I drew them, with ropes of love, \q and I was to them like those who lift a yoke off their jaws, \q and I bent down to him [and] fed [him].
en.B: I led them with human cords, with ropes of love. \q To them I was like someone who lifts the yoke off their jaws, \q and I bent down to them and fed them.
en.R: I led them with cords of kindness, the kind used for people, with ropes of love. \q I was like someone who eases the yoke on an animal's jaws. \q I bent down to them and fed them.

es.L: Con cuerdas humanas los atraje, con lazos de amor, \q y fui para ellos como los que alzan el yugo de sobre sus quijadas, \q y me incliné hacia él [y le] di de comer.
es.B: Los guie con cuerdas humanas, con lazos de amor. \q Fui para ellos como quien les quita el yugo de las quijadas, \q y me incliné hacia ellos y les di de comer.
es.R: Los guie con cuerdas de bondad, de las que se usan para las personas, con lazos de amor. \q Fui como quien afloja el yugo en las quijadas de un animal. \q Me incliné hacia ellos y les di de comer.

fr.L: Avec des cordes humaines je les ai tirés, avec des liens d’amour, \q et j’ai été pour eux comme ceux qui soulèvent le joug de dessus leurs mâchoires, \q et je me suis penché vers lui [et je l’ai] nourri.
fr.B: Je les ai conduits avec des cordes humaines, avec des liens d’amour. \q J’ai été pour eux comme quelqu’un qui leur ôte le joug des mâchoires, \q et je me suis penché vers eux pour les nourrir.
fr.R: Je les ai conduits avec des cordes de bonté, celles qu’on utilise pour les personnes, avec des liens d’amour. \q J’ai été comme quelqu’un qui desserre le joug sur les mâchoires d’un animal. \q Je me suis penché vers eux et je les ai nourris.

sw.L: Kwa kamba za binadamu niliwavuta, kwa kamba za upendo, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nilikuwa kwao kama wale wanaoinua nira kutoka mataya yao, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nikainama kwake [na] kumlisha.
sw.B: Niliwaongoza kwa kamba za kibinadamu, kwa kamba za upendo. \q Kwao nilikuwa kama mtu anayeinua nira kutoka mataya yao, \q nikainama kwao na kuwalisha.
sw.R: Niliwaongoza kwa kamba za wema, zile zinazotumiwa kwa watu, kwa kamba za upendo. \q Nilikuwa kama mtu anayelegeza nira kwenye mataya ya mnyama. \q Niliinama kwao na kuwalisha.

vi.L: Bằng dây của loài người {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã kéo chúng, bằng thừng của tình yêu, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối với chúng như những người nhấc ách khỏi hàm chúng, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cúi xuống với nó [và] cho [nó] ăn.
vi.B: Ta đã dắt chúng bằng dây của con người, bằng dây yêu thương. \q Đối với chúng, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} như người nhấc ách khỏi hàm chúng, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cúi xuống cho chúng ăn.
vi.R: Ta đã dắt chúng bằng dây nhân từ, loại dây dùng cho con người, bằng dây yêu thương. \q Ta như người nới ách trên hàm một con vật. \q Ta cúi xuống cho chúng ăn.

ko.L: 내가 사람의 줄로, 사랑의 끈으로 그들을 이끌었다. \q 나는 그들에게 그들의 턱에서 멍에를 들어 올려 주는 자와 같았고, \q 그에게 몸을 굽혀 [그를] 먹였다.
ko.B: 나는 사람을 이끄는 줄로, 사랑의 끈으로 그들을 이끌었다. \q 나는 그들에게 턱에서 멍에를 벗겨 주는 사람과 같았고, \q 몸을 굽혀 그들을 먹여 주었다.
ko.R: 나는 사람에게 쓰는 부드러운 줄로, 사랑의 끈으로 그들을 이끌었다. \q 나는 짐승의 턱에 걸린 멍에를 느슨하게 해 주는 사람과 같았다. \q 나는 몸을 굽혀 그들을 먹여 주었다.

decisions.choice: cords of a human, ropes of love: God led Israel by gentle means fit for people, not by force
decisions.reason: "Cords of a human" are cords suited to human beings, set beside "ropes of love". God did not drive Israel like a beast but drew them with kindness. The words prepare for the picture that follows, where the cords that might bind an animal are loosened.

decisions.choice: like those who lift a yoke off their jaws: a farmer easing the yoke so that the animal can eat
alternatives: like those who lift an infant to their cheeks (a reading that changes only the vowels of the word for "yoke")
decisions.reason: As the Hebrew is written, God is like a farmer who loosens or raises the yoke from an ox's jaws, so that it can rest and feed; "I bent down and fed him" then follows naturally. With different vowels, the same letters can mean "infant", giving the picture of a parent lifting a baby to the cheek, which suits verses 1 and 3. The written vowels are followed; the line is uncertain.

decisions.choice: I bent down to him and fed him: God stooping to feed his people
decisions.reason: The word read as "I bent down" may also be read as "gently". Either way God stoops to feed the one he leads. "Him" is Ephraim as one person, the child of verse 1. The feeding recalls the manna in the wilderness (Exodus 16).

decisions.choice: cords of kindness, the kind used for people ... an animal's jaws (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says what "cords of a human" means (m1) and makes clear that the yoke picture is about a working animal (m2). It follows the reading chosen in m2.

decisions.choice: [and] fed [him] (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has two verbs side by side, "I bent down to him, I fed", with no "and" and no object; Literal brackets both.

decisions.choice: to them ... fed them (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "him" for Ephraim as one person (m3). Balanced and Readable say "them", as in the first half of the verse, so the reader does not look for a new person.

decisions.choice: "cuerdas humanas" (L, B); "cuerdas de bondad, de las que se usan para las personas" (R); "lazos de amor"
decisions.reason: The picture of gentle leading, drafted from the Hebrew; Readable explains it, as the English Readable does.

source.text: לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר ה֣וּא מַלְכּ֑וֹ כִּ֥י מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: Not he will return to [the] land of Egypt, and Assyria, he [will be] his king, for they refused to return.

en.L: He will not return to the land of Egypt, \q but Assyria, he [will be] his king, \q because they refused to return.
en.B: He will not go back to the land of Egypt; \q Assyria will be his king instead, \q because they refused to return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: They will not go back to Egypt. \q Instead, the king of Assyria will rule over them, \q because they refused to come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: No volverá a la tierra de Egipto, \q sino que Asiria, ella [será] su rey, \q porque se negaron a volver.
es.B: No volverá a la tierra de Egipto; \q Asiria será su rey en cambio, \q porque se negaron a volverse a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: No volverán a Egipto. \q En cambio, el rey de Asiria los gobernará, \q porque se negaron a volver a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

fr.L: Il ne reviendra pas au pays d’Égypte, \q mais l’Assyrie, elle [sera] son roi, \q parce qu’ils ont refusé de revenir.
fr.B: Il ne reviendra pas au pays d’Égypte ; \q c’est l’Assyrie qui sera son roi, \q parce qu’ils ont refusé de revenir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Ils ne reviendront pas en Égypte. \q Au contraire, le roi d’Assyrie régnera sur eux, \q parce qu’ils ont refusé de revenir à {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.

sw.L: Hatarudi katika nchi ya Misri, \q bali Ashuru, yeye [atakuwa] mfalme wake, \q kwa sababu walikataa kurudi.
sw.B: Hatarudi katika nchi ya Misri; \q badala yake Ashuru atakuwa mfalme wake, \q kwa sababu walikataa kurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.
sw.R: Hawatarudi Misri. \q Badala yake, mfalme wa Ashuru atawatawala, \q kwa sababu walikataa kurudi {{deity_pronoun:kwangu|Kwangu}}.

vi.L: Nó sẽ không trở về đất Ai Cập, \q nhưng A-si-ri, chính nó [sẽ là] vua của nó, \q vì chúng đã từ chối trở về.
vi.B: Nó sẽ không trở lại đất Ai Cập; \q thay vào đó A-si-ri sẽ làm vua nó, \q vì chúng đã không chịu quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Chúng sẽ không trở lại Ai Cập. \q Thay vào đó, vua A-si-ri sẽ cai trị chúng, \q vì chúng đã không chịu quay về với {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

ko.L: 그는 이집트 땅으로 돌아가지 않을 것이다. \q 그러나 앗시리아, 그가 그의 왕이 [될 것이다]. \q 그들이 돌아오기를 거절했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그는 이집트 땅으로 돌아가지 않을 것이다. \q 오히려 앗시리아가 그의 왕이 될 것이다. \q 그들이 나에게 돌아오기를 거절했기 때문이다.
ko.R: 그들은 이집트로 돌아가지 않을 것이다. \q 오히려 앗시리아 왕이 그들을 다스릴 것이다. \q 그들이 나에게 돌아오기를 거절했기 때문이다.

decisions.choice: He will not return to Egypt: Egypt will be no refuge; Assyria will rule him
alternatives: He will return to Egypt (reading the first word as "to him" and joining it to verse 4, as 8:13 and 9:3 say)
a question: Will he not return to the land of Egypt?
decisions.reason: As written, the verse says that Ephraim will not go back to Egypt, the land of its slavery and the power it looked to for help (7:11; 12:2); Assyria will be its master instead. Hosea also says that "they will return to Egypt" (8:13; 9:3), so some read the first word, which sounds the same as "to him", as the end of verse 4, or take the line as a question. The words as written are followed.

decisions.choice: return ... refused to return: a play on the verb "turn back"
decisions.reason: The same verb is used twice. Ephraim will not turn back to Egypt, because it would not turn back to God. To "return" is Hosea's word for repentance (3:5; 6:1; 14:2).

decisions.choice: Assyria will be his king: the northern kingdom under Assyrian rule
decisions.reason: The last kings of Israel paid tribute to Assyria, and when King Hoshea turned to Egypt for help, Assyria took Samaria and carried the people away (2 Kings 17:3-6), in 722 BC.

decisions.choice: return to me (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom Israel refused to return to, which the Hebrew leaves implied (m2). God is the speaker, so "me" takes the deity pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: the king of Assyria will rule over them (R)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the picture of a nation as king into plain words, and uses "they" for Ephraim, as it does through the chapter.

source.text: וְחָלָ֥ה חֶ֨רֶב֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְכִלְּתָ֥ה בַדָּ֖יו וְאָכָ֑לָה מִֽמֹּעֲצ֖וֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And will whirl [the] sword in his cities, and will finish his bars, and will devour, because of their counsels.

en.L: And the sword will whirl in his cities \q and put an end to his bars and devour [them], \q because of their schemes.
en.B: A sword will sweep through their cities; \q it will break the bars of their gates and consume them, \q because of their own schemes.
en.R: Swords will sweep through their cities. \q They will smash the bars of their gates and destroy the people, \q because of the plans they made.

es.L: Y la espada girará en sus ciudades \q y acabará con sus cerrojos y [los] devorará, \q a causa de sus intrigas.
es.B: La espada arrasará sus ciudades; \q romperá los cerrojos de sus puertas y los consumirá, \q a causa de sus propias intrigas.
es.R: Las espadas arrasarán sus ciudades. \q Romperán los cerrojos de sus puertas y destruirán a la gente, \q a causa de los planes que hicieron.

fr.L: Et l’épée tournoiera dans ses villes, \q et elle mettra fin à ses verrous et [les] dévorera, \q à cause de leurs desseins.
fr.B: L’épée balaiera leurs villes ; \q elle brisera les verrous de leurs portes et les dévorera, \q à cause de leurs propres manœuvres.
fr.R: Les épées balaieront leurs villes. \q Elles briseront les verrous de leurs portes et détruiront les gens, \q à cause des plans qu’ils ont faits.

sw.L: Na upanga utazunguka katika miji yake \q na kuyakomesha makomeo yake na kula [watu], \q kwa sababu ya mashauri yao.
sw.B: Upanga utapita kwa kasi katika miji yao; \q utavunja makomeo ya malango yao na kuwaangamiza, \q kwa sababu ya hila zao wenyewe.
sw.R: Panga zitapita kwa kasi katika miji yao. \q Zitavunja makomeo ya malango yao na kuwaua watu, \q kwa sababu ya mipango waliyoifanya.

vi.L: Và gươm sẽ vung lên trong các thành nó \q và hủy diệt các then cửa nó và nuốt [chúng], \q vì những mưu kế của chúng.
vi.B: Gươm sẽ quét qua các thành của chúng; \q nó sẽ bẻ gãy then cổng thành và tiêu diệt chúng, \q vì chính mưu kế của chúng.
vi.R: Gươm giáo sẽ quét qua các thành của chúng. \q Gươm giáo sẽ phá gãy then cổng và giết hại dân chúng, \q vì những kế hoạch chúng đã bày ra.

ko.L: 칼이 그의 성읍들에서 휘몰아치고, \q 그의 빗장들을 끝장내고 [그들을] 삼킬 것이다. \q 그들의 계략 때문이다.
ko.B: 칼이 그들의 성읍들을 휩쓸고, \q 성문 빗장들을 부수고 그들을 삼킬 것이다. \q 그들 자신의 계략 때문이다.
ko.R: 칼이 그들의 성읍들을 휩쓸 것이다. \q 성문 빗장들을 부수고 백성을 죽일 것이다. \q 그들이 세운 계획 때문이다.

decisions.choice: his bars: the bars that bolt the city gates
alternatives: his empty talkers (the same letters form a word for boasters or false prophets, Isaiah 44:25; Jeremiah 50:36)
decisions.reason: The word can mean the bars or poles that bolt a gate (Job 17:16; compare Job 18:13), which suits a sword raging through cities. The same letters also spell a word for idle talkers or diviners, which would fit "their schemes". The first sense is followed.

decisions.choice: the sword will whirl: war will rage through the land
decisions.reason: The verb means to whirl or to writhe. The sword, standing for an invading army, swings and flashes as it goes through the cities.

decisions.choice: their schemes: the plans they made, above all their alliances
decisions.reason: The word means counsel or plans. Ephraim's leaders schemed to save themselves by treaties with Egypt and Assyria (7:11; 12:2), and the plans themselves bring the sword.

decisions.choice: the bars of their gates ... consume them (B); destroy the people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the bars are (m1) and supply the object of "devour". They use "their" for Ephraim's "his", since the people are meant.

source.text: וְעַמִּ֥י תְלוּאִ֖ים לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִ֑י וְאֶל־עַל֙ יִקְרָאֻ֔הוּ יַ֖חַד לֹ֥א יְרוֹמֵם׃

records.literal_gloss: And my people [are] hung on turning from me; and to [the] height they call him; together not he lifts up.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people are bent on turning away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q and to [the One] on high they call him, \q [but] none at all rises up.
en.B: My people are set on turning away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q Though they are called to the One on high, \q not one of them rises up.
en.R: My people are determined to turn away from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q They are called to come up to God Most High, \q but not one of them gets up to come.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} pueblo está empeñado en apartarse de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; \q y al Altísimo lo llaman, \q [pero] ninguno en absoluto se levanta.
es.B: Mi pueblo está decidido a apartarse de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Aunque los llaman hacia el Altísimo, \q ninguno de ellos se levanta.
es.R: Mi pueblo está decidido a alejarse de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Se les llama a subir hacia el Dios Altísimo, \q pero ninguno se levanta para venir.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} peuple est attaché à se détourner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q et vers [Celui d’]en haut on l’appelle, \q [mais] aucun ne se lève.
fr.B: Mon peuple est décidé à se détourner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q On a beau l’appeler vers Celui d’en haut, \q pas un seul ne se lève.
fr.R: Mon peuple est résolu à s’éloigner de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q On les appelle à monter vers le Dieu Très-Haut, \q mais pas un seul ne se lève pour venir.

sw.L: Na watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wameshikamana na kuniacha; \q na kwa [Yeye aliye] juu wanamwita, \q [lakini] hakuna hata mmoja anayeinuka.
sw.B: Watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wamekaza nia kuniacha. \q Ingawa wanaitwa kwa Yeye aliye juu, \q hakuna hata mmoja wao anayeinuka.
sw.R: Watu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wameamua kuniacha. \q Wanaitwa waje kwa Mungu Aliye Juu Kabisa, \q lakini hakuna hata mmoja anayeinuka kuja.

vi.L: Và dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cứ khăng khăng quay lìa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q và người ta gọi nó đến cùng [Đấng] trên cao, \q [nhưng] chẳng có ai chỗi dậy.
vi.B: Dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} quyết tâm quay lìa {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Dù được kêu gọi đến cùng Đấng ở trên cao, \q chẳng một ai trong chúng chỗi dậy.
vi.R: Dân {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nhất quyết bỏ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng được kêu gọi đến với Đức Chúa Trời Chí Cao, \q nhưng chẳng một ai đứng dậy mà đến.

ko.L: 내 백성은 나에게서 돌아서는 데 매달려 있다. \q 그들을 높은 곳으로 부르지만, \q 아무도 일어나지 않는다.
ko.B: 내 백성은 나에게서 돌아서기로 마음을 굳혔다. \q 그들을 높은 곳에 있는 이에게로 부르지만, \q 그들 가운데 아무도 일어나지 않는다.
ko.R: 내 백성은 나에게서 등을 돌리기로 작정했다. \q 가장 높은 하나님에게로 올라오라고 그들을 부르지만, \q 그들 가운데 아무도 일어나 오지 않는다.

decisions.choice: hung on: fixed on, set on
decisions.reason: The verb means to hang or to be hung. Here it pictures a people whose hearts are hung on, fixed on, turning away. It is used in Deuteronomy 28:66 of a life that "hangs in doubt", so some take it as wavering; the next lines suggest a settled refusal.

decisions.choice: turning away from me: unfaithfulness to God
decisions.reason: The noun comes from the verb "turn", like "return" in verse 5. Hosea uses it of Israel's backsliding, and God promises to heal it (14:5; compare Jeremiah 3:22).

decisions.choice: they are called upward, to the One on high, but not one of them rises: the people will not answer the call
alternatives: they call to the Most High, but he will not raise them up at all
they call him to a false god (reading the word for "on high" as a name)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of this line is among the hardest in the book, and every translation is a guess. "They call him" most likely continues verse 2, where messengers called Israel. The word for "on high" is the one in 7:16, "they turn, but not upward", and here may mean God Most High. The last words, "together he does not lift up", are taken as "not one rises". Taken another way, the line says that the people call to God but he will not lift them up.

decisions.choice: they are called (B, R); gets up to come (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "they are called", since the callers are the messengers of verse 2 and the one called is Israel. Readable puts "does not lift up" as not getting up to come. Both follow the reading chosen in m3.

decisions.choice: "al Altísimo" (L, B); "el Dios Altísimo" (R)
alternatives: a Aquel que está en lo alto
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "upward" points to God on high; Spanish names him with the published title, where the English has "the One on high".

decisions.choice: "높은 곳에 있는 이" (B), "가장 높은 하나님" (R), without -시-
decisions.reason: God is speaking of himself, so the English "the One on high" takes no honorific in his mouth.

source.text: אֵ֞יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ אֶפְרַ֗יִם אֲמַגֶּנְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ כְאַדְמָ֔ה אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כִּצְבֹאיִ֑ם נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לִבִּ֔י יַ֖חַד נִכְמְר֥וּ נִחוּמָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: How will I give you up, Ephraim? [How] will I hand you over, Israel? How will I make you like Admah? [How] will I set you like Zeboiim? Is turned over within me my heart; together are kindled my compassions.

en.L: How can I give you up, Ephraim? [How can] I surrender you, Israel? \q How can I treat you like Admah? \q [How can] I set you like Zeboiim? \q My heart is turned over within {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}; \q all together {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} compassion grows warm.
en.B: How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I surrender you, Israel? \q How can I treat you like Admah? \q How can I make you like Zeboiim? \q Within {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} heart turns over; \q all {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} compassion is stirred.
en.R: Ephraim, how can I give you up? Israel, how can I hand you over to your enemies? \q How can I destroy you as I destroyed Admah? \q How can I treat you like Zeboiim? Those towns were wiped out with Sodom. \q My heart is turned upside down within {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q All {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} tender love for you is stirred up.

es.L: ¿Cómo podré entregarte, Efraín? ¿[Cómo podré] abandonarte, Israel? \q ¿Cómo podré tratarte como a Adma? \q ¿[Cómo podré] ponerte como a Zeboim? \q Mi corazón se revuelve dentro de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}; \q toda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} compasión se enciende.
es.B: ¿Cómo podré abandonarte, Efraín? ¿Cómo podré entregarte, Israel? \q ¿Cómo podré tratarte como a Adma? \q ¿Cómo podré hacerte como a Zeboim? \q Dentro de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} se revuelve {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} corazón; \q toda {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} compasión se conmueve.
es.R: Efraín, ¿cómo podré abandonarte? Israel, ¿cómo podré entregarte a tus enemigos? \q ¿Cómo podré destruirte como destruí a Adma? \q ¿Cómo podré tratarte como a Zeboim? Esas ciudades fueron destruidas junto con Sodoma. \q Mi corazón está trastornado dentro de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Todo {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierno amor por ti se conmueve.

fr.L: Comment pourrais-je te livrer, Éphraïm ? [Comment pourrais-je] te céder, Israël ? \q Comment pourrais-je te traiter comme Adma ? \q [Comment pourrais-je] te rendre comme Tseboïm ? \q Mon cœur se retourne en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} ; \q {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} compassion tout entière s’échauffe.
fr.B: Comment pourrais-je t’abandonner, Éphraïm ? Comment pourrais-je te livrer, Israël ? \q Comment pourrais-je te traiter comme Adma ? \q Comment pourrais-je te rendre pareil à Tseboïm ? \q En {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} cœur est bouleversé ; \q toute {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} compassion s’émeut.
fr.R: Éphraïm, comment pourrais-je t’abandonner ? Israël, comment pourrais-je te livrer à tes ennemis ? \q Comment pourrais-je te détruire comme j’ai détruit Adma ? \q Comment pourrais-je te traiter comme Tseboïm ? Ces villes ont été anéanties avec Sodome. \q Mon cœur est tout retourné en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Tout {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} tendre amour pour toi se réveille.

sw.L: Nitakutoaje, Efraimu? [Nitakukabidhije], Israeli? \q Nitakufanyaje kama Adma? \q [Nitakuwekaje] kama Seboimu? \q Moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umegeuka ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q huruma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote pamoja inawaka.
sw.B: Ninawezaje kukuacha, Efraimu? Ninawezaje kukukabidhi, Israeli? \q Ninawezaje kukutendea kama Adma? \q Ninawezaje kukufanya kama Seboimu? \q Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} unageuka; \q huruma {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} yote inaamka.
sw.R: Efraimu, ninawezaje kukuacha? Israeli, ninawezaje kukutia mikononi mwa adui zako? \q Ninawezaje kukuangamiza kama nilivyoiangamiza Adma? \q Ninawezaje kukutendea kama Seboimu? Miji hiyo iliangamizwa pamoja na Sodoma. \q Moyo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} umevurugika ndani {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Upendo {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} wote wa huruma kwako umeamshwa.

vi.L: Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bỏ ngươi được, hỡi Ép-ra-im? [Làm sao] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nộp ngươi được, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên? \q Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối xử với ngươi như Át-ma? \q [Làm sao] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đặt ngươi như Sê-bô-im? \q Lòng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đảo lộn trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cùng nhau nóng lên.
vi.B: Hỡi Ép-ra-im, làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bỏ con được? Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trao con đi được? \q Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối xử với con như Át-ma? \q Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} làm cho con giống như Sê-bô-im? \q Trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, lòng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} quặn thắt; \q tất cả lòng thương xót của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trỗi dậy.
vi.R: Hỡi Ép-ra-im, làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bỏ con được? Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} giao con cho kẻ thù được? \q Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} hủy diệt con như {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã hủy diệt Át-ma? \q Làm sao {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đối xử với con như Sê-bô-im? Các thành ấy đã bị xóa sạch cùng với Sô-đôm. \q Lòng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đảo lộn trong {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Cả tình thương dịu dàng của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} dành cho con đều trỗi dậy.

ko.L: 에브라임아, 내가 어찌 너를 내주겠느냐? 이스라엘아, 내가 어찌 너를 넘기겠느냐? \q 내가 어찌 너를 아드마처럼 만들겠느냐? \q 내가 어찌 너를 스보임처럼 두겠느냐? \q 내 마음이 내 속에서 뒤집히고, \q 내 긍휼이 한꺼번에 뜨거워진다.
ko.B: 에브라임아, 내가 어떻게 너를 포기하겠느냐? 이스라엘아, 내가 어떻게 너를 내주겠느냐? \q 내가 어떻게 너를 아드마처럼 대하겠느냐? \q 내가 어떻게 너를 스보임처럼 만들겠느냐? \q 내 마음이 속에서 뒤집히고, \q 나의 긍휼이 온통 끓어오른다.
ko.R: 에브라임아, 내가 어떻게 너를 버리겠느냐? 이스라엘아, 내가 어떻게 너를 원수들에게 넘겨주겠느냐? \q 내가 아드마를 멸망시킨 것처럼 어떻게 너를 멸망시키겠느냐? \q 내가 어떻게 너를 스보임처럼 대하겠느냐? 그 성읍들은 소돔과 함께 망했다. \q 내 마음이 속에서 뒤집힌다. \q 너를 향한 나의 자비로운 사랑이 온통 끓어오른다.

decisions.choice: Admah and Zeboiim: the cities destroyed with Sodom and Gomorrah
decisions.reason: Admah and Zeboiim were cities of the plain, named with Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 10:19; 14:2) and destroyed with them (Genesis 19:24-25). Deuteronomy 29:22 names all four as the picture of the curse that would fall on Israel if it broke the covenant: a land burned out "like the overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah, Admah and Zeboiim". Hosea names the two lesser cities. Ephraim deserves their fate, and God asks how he can give it.

decisions.choice: my heart is turned over: the same verb as the "overthrow" of those cities
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for the overthrow of Sodom and the other cities (Genesis 19:25; Deuteronomy 29:22). Instead of overturning Ephraim, God's own heart is overturned. The heart is the seat of thought and will, so the words describe a change of purpose as well as deep feeling.

decisions.choice: my compassion grows warm: tender love stirred to its depths
decisions.reason: The same phrase is used of Joseph, whose "compassion grew warm" for his brother (Genesis 43:30), and of the mother who would rather lose her son than see him killed (1 Kings 3:26). The word for compassion is related to the word for womb. God's love for Ephraim is the love of a parent for a child.

decisions.choice: How can I ...? Questions of anguish, not of doubt about God's power
decisions.reason: God is able to give Ephraim up, and Ephraim deserves it (verses 5-7). The questions say how much it costs God to think of it. Verse 9 gives the answer: he will not.

decisions.choice: [How can] (L); How can (B)
decisions.reason: In the Hebrew, "how" is written only before the first and third questions and carries over to the second and fourth. Literal brackets the words carried over; Balanced repeats them.

decisions.choice: hand you over to your enemies ... destroy you as I destroyed Admah ... Those towns were wiped out with Sodom (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom Ephraim would be handed over, what being made like Admah would mean, and who Admah and Zeboiim were (m1), so that a reader who does not know the names can follow.

decisions.choice: compassion (L, B); tender love (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew noun is plural, a common way of speaking of deep feelings. English says "compassion". Readable says "tender love" to keep the warmth of the word (m3).

decisions.choice: "Adma", "Zeboim"
decisions.reason: The published Spanish forms (Genesis 10:19; Deuteronomy 29:22).

decisions.choice: "se revuelve" (L, B); "está trastornado" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the overthrow of the cities of the plain; Spanish gives the heart's turmoil, and the meaning decision notes the echo.

decisions.choice: God says "con" to Ephraim in 11:8-9 (B, R); "ngươi" (L)
decisions.reason: The settled Vietnamese address uses "con" at Balanced and Readable in the tender passages of Hosea, and these two verses are God's cry of love; Literal keeps "ngươi".

decisions.choice: "뒤집히다" for the heart; *nichumim* "긍휼" (L, B), "자비로운 사랑" (R)
decisions.reason: "뒤집히다" keeps the link with the overthrow of the cities that the shared decision notes; the compassion is worded fresh rather than with the familiar older lines.

source.text: לֹ֤א אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ חֲר֣וֹן אַפִּ֔י לֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב לְשַׁחֵ֣ת אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל אָֽנֹכִי֙ וְלֹא־אִ֔ישׁ בְּקִרְבְּךָ֣ קָד֔וֹשׁ וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וֹא בְּעִֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: Not I will carry out [the] burning of my anger; not I will return to destroy Ephraim; for God I [am] and not a man, in your midst [the] Holy One, and not I will come in wrath.

en.L: I will not carry out the burning of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger; \q I will not again destroy Ephraim; \q for I [am] God and not {{gender:a human|a man}}, \q the Holy One in your midst, \q and I will not come in wrath.
en.B: I will not act on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} burning anger; \q I will not turn to destroy Ephraim again. \q For I am God and not {{gender:a human|a man}}, \q the Holy One among you, \q and I will not come in fury.
en.R: I will not let {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fierce anger loose on you. \q I will not destroy Ephraim again. \q I am God, not a human being. \q I am the Holy One who lives among you. \q I will not come to you in anger.

es.L: No ejecutaré el ardor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira; \q no volveré a destruir a Efraín; \q porque Dios [soy] yo, y no {{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}}, \q el Santo en medio de ti, \q y no vendré con furor.
es.B: No daré rienda suelta al ardor de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira; \q no volveré a destruir a Efraín. \q Porque yo soy Dios, y no {{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}}, \q el Santo en medio de ti, \q y no vendré con furor.
es.R: No dejaré que {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira ardiente caiga sobre ti. \q No volveré a destruir a Efraín. \q Yo soy Dios, no un ser humano. \q Soy el Santo que vive en medio de ti. \q No vendré a ti con enojo.

fr.L: Je n’exécuterai pas l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; \q je ne reviendrai pas détruire Éphraïm ; \q car je [suis] Dieu et non {{gender:un être humain|un homme}}, \q le Saint au milieu de toi, \q et je ne viendrai pas avec fureur.
fr.B: Je ne donnerai pas libre cours à l’ardeur de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ; \q je ne reviendrai pas détruire Éphraïm. \q Car je suis Dieu et non {{gender:un être humain|un homme}}, \q le Saint au milieu de toi, \q et je ne viendrai pas avec fureur.
fr.R: Je ne laisserai pas éclater sur toi {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère ardente. \q Je ne détruirai plus Éphraïm. \q Je suis Dieu, pas un être humain. \q Je suis le Saint qui vit au milieu de toi. \q Je ne viendrai pas vers toi avec colère.

sw.L: Sitautekeleza moto wa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}; \q sitarudi kumharibu Efraimu; \q kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] Mungu, si binadamu, \q Yule Mtakatifu aliye katikati yako, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} sitakuja kwa ghadhabu kali.
sw.B: Sitatenda kwa hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} iwakayo; \q sitageuka kumwangamiza Efraimu tena. \q Kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni Mungu, si binadamu, \q Yule Mtakatifu aliye kati yako, \q na sitakuja kwa ghadhabu.
sw.R: Sitakumwagia hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kali. \q Sitamwangamiza Efraimu tena. \q Mimi ni Mungu, si binadamu. \q Mimi ndiye Mtakatifu anayeishi kati yako. \q Sitakujia kwa hasira.

vi.L: Ta sẽ không thi hành cơn giận nóng cháy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không trở lại hủy diệt Ép-ra-im; \q vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] Đức Chúa Trời, không phải loài người, \q là Đấng Thánh ở giữa ngươi, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không đến trong cơn thịnh nộ.
vi.B: Ta sẽ không để cơn giận nóng cháy của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} bùng lên; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không quay lại hủy diệt Ép-ra-im nữa. \q Vì {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đức Chúa Trời, không phải là người phàm, \q là Đấng Thánh ở giữa con, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ không đến trong cơn thịnh nộ.
vi.R: Ta sẽ không trút cơn giận dữ dội của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} trên con. \q Ta sẽ không hủy diệt Ép-ra-im nữa. \q Ta là Đức Chúa Trời, chứ không phải loài người. \q Ta là Đấng Thánh sống giữa con. \q Ta sẽ không đến với con trong cơn giận.

ko.L: 나는 내 분노의 불길을 쏟지 않겠다. \q 다시는 에브라임을 멸하지 않겠다. \q 나는 하나님이지 사람이 아니기 때문이다. \q 나는 너희 가운데 있는 거룩한 이다. \q 나는 진노하며 오지 않겠다.
ko.B: 나는 불타는 내 진노대로 하지 않겠다. \q 다시 돌이켜 에브라임을 멸하지 않겠다. \q 나는 하나님이지 사람이 아니다. \q 나는 너희 가운데 있는 거룩한 이다. \q 나는 진노하며 오지 않겠다.
ko.R: 나는 맹렬한 분노를 너희에게 쏟지 않겠다. \q 나는 에브라임을 다시 멸망시키지 않겠다. \q 나는 하나님이지 사람이 아니다. \q 나는 너희 가운데 사는 거룩한 이다. \q 나는 분노하며 너희에게 가지 않겠다.

decisions.choice: I am God and not a man: God's holiness shows itself in mercy
decisions.reason: A human being in such anger would strike, and Ephraim has earned it. God is not bound to act as people do. Being God, "the Holy One", wholly other than humans, is the reason he holds back. The same contrast is used in Numbers 23:19 and 1 Samuel 15:29, where it says that God does not lie or change his mind as people do; here it says that he will not destroy as people would.

decisions.choice: a man: a human being, set against God
decisions.reason: The word usually means a man. Set against "God", it means any human being, man or woman, as in Numbers 23:19. The point is the difference between God and humankind, not between God and men.

decisions.choice: I will not again destroy: there will be no second Admah
alternatives: I will not turn back to destroy ("turn" meaning a change of course)
decisions.reason: The verb "return" is often used to mean "do again". God will not repeat the overthrow of verse 8 on Ephraim. It can also mean that God will not turn around to destroy. Either way the threat of verse 8 is withdrawn.

decisions.choice: in wrath
alternatives: into a city (the same letters spell the common word for "city")
decisions.reason: The last word can be read as "in wrath", matching "the burning of my anger" at the start of the verse, or as "into a city", as if God would not come to destroy a city. The first reading is followed.

decisions.choice: not a human (L, B, with "a man" as the gender setting's alternative); not a human being (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew means a human being here (m2), so Literal and Balanced use the gender setting, with the inclusive word as the default and the traditional "a man" as the alternative, as Numbers 23:19 does. Readable says "a human being", which is already inclusive and needs no setting. God is never given a gender span.

decisions.choice: act on my burning anger (B); let my fierce anger loose on you (R)
alternatives: carry out the burning of my anger
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put the Hebrew phrase in natural English; Literal keeps "carry out the burning of my anger".

decisions.choice: "{{gender:un ser humano|un hombre}}"
decisions.reason: Here Spanish has two wordings as the English does: "un ser humano" by default, "un hombre" as the gender setting's alternative. Readable says "un ser humano" plainly, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "furor" (L, B); "enojo" (R)
decisions.reason: Wrath as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:un être humain|un homme}}" (L, B); "un être humain" (R)
decisions.reason: French has two wordings here, as the English does, so Literal and Balanced carry the gender setting; Readable's "un être humain" needs none.

decisions.choice: "si binadamu" with no gender span
decisions.reason: "binadamu" already means a human being of either sex, so the English gender setting has nothing to change in Swahili.

decisions.choice: "사람" with no gender span; "너희 가운데 있는 거룩한 이", without -시-
decisions.reason: Korean "사람" already means a human being, so the gender span has no second wording; God names himself "거룩한 이" as in Isaiah.

source.text: אַחֲרֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה יֵלְכ֖וּ כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה יִשְׁאָ֑ג כִּֽי־ה֣וּא יִשְׁאַ֔ג וְיֶחֶרְד֥וּ בָנִ֖ים מִיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: After Yahweh they will walk; like a lion he will roar; for he, he will roar, and will come trembling [the] children from [the] west.

en.L: After {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} they will walk; like a lion {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will roar; \q for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will roar, \q and {{gender:children|sons}} will come trembling from the west.
en.B: They will follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who will roar like a lion. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} roars, \q {{gender:children|sons}} will come trembling from the west.
en.R: The people will follow {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who will roar like a lion. \q When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} roars, \q they will come back from the west, trembling.

es.L: En pos {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} andarán; como león rugirá; \q porque {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} rugirá, \q y vendrán temblando hijos desde el occidente.
es.B: Seguirán {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que rugirá como un león. \q Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ruja, \q los hijos vendrán temblando desde el occidente.
es.R: El pueblo seguirá {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, que rugirá como un león. \q Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ruja, \q volverán temblando desde el occidente.

fr.L: Ils marcheront derrière {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ; comme un lion {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rugira ; \q car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rugira, \q et des {{gender:enfants|fils}} viendront en tremblant de l’occident.
fr.B: Ils suivront {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui rugira comme un lion. \q Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rugira, \q des {{gender:enfants|fils}} accourront en tremblant de l’occident.
fr.R: Le peuple suivra {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, qui rugira comme un lion. \q Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} rugira, \q ils reviendront de l’occident en tremblant.

sw.L: Watatembea nyuma ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; kama simba atanguruma; \q kwa maana {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} atanguruma, \q na watoto watakuja wakitetemeka kutoka magharibi.
sw.B: Watamfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, atakayenguruma kama simba. \q Atakaponguruma, \q watoto watakuja wakitetemeka kutoka magharibi.
sw.R: Watu watamfuata {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, atakayenguruma kama simba. \q Atakaponguruma, \q watarudi kutoka magharibi wakitetemeka.

vi.L: Họ sẽ bước theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ gầm như sư tử; \q vì chính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} sẽ gầm, \q và con cái sẽ run rẩy kéo đến từ phương tây.
vi.B: Họ sẽ đi theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đấng sẽ gầm như sư tử. \q Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gầm lên, \q con cái sẽ run rẩy kéo đến từ phương tây.
vi.R: Dân chúng sẽ đi theo {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, Đấng sẽ gầm như sư tử. \q Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} gầm lên, \q họ sẽ run rẩy trở về từ phương tây.

ko.L: 그들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 따라 걸을 것이다. 그분께서 사자처럼 부르짖으실 것이다. \q 그분께서 부르짖으시면 \q {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이 서쪽에서 떨며 올 것이다.
ko.B: 그들은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 따라갈 것이다. 그분께서 사자처럼 부르짖으실 것이다. \q 그분께서 부르짖으시면 \q {{gender:자녀|아들}}들이 서쪽에서 떨며 달려올 것이다.
ko.R: 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 따라갈 것이다. 그분께서 사자처럼 부르짖으실 것이다. \q 그분께서 부르짖으시면 \q 그들이 서쪽에서 떨며 돌아올 것이다.

decisions.choice: they will walk after the LORD: the people will follow God; the prophet speaks of God for a moment
decisions.reason: To walk after someone is to follow and obey him (Deuteronomy 13:5). God, who has spoken as "I" through the chapter, is named here, and in verse 11 speaks as "I" again. Such changes of voice are common in the prophets.

decisions.choice: roar like a lion: here a call that brings the scattered home
decisions.reason: Elsewhere the lion's roar is a picture of judgment (5:14; 13:7; Amos 1:2; 3:8). Here the same roar is a summons: when God calls, his people come back.

decisions.choice: come trembling from the west: hurry home in awe, from across the sea
decisions.reason: The verb means to tremble, and with "from" it pictures people hurrying, shaken, as birds flutter (verse 11). "The west" is literally "the sea", the Mediterranean, which lies west of the land; the scattered will come back from every side.

decisions.choice: children, with "sons" as the gender setting's alternative (L, B); they (R)
decisions.reason: The word is "sons", meaning the people of Israel, men and women, so it takes the gender setting. Readable says "they" for the people named at the start of its sentence.

decisions.choice: "hijos", with no gender span
decisions.reason: Spanish "hijos" already includes daughters.

decisions.choice: The prophet speaks of God for a moment, so God takes -시- ("부르짖으실")
decisions.reason: As the shared meaning decision says, this verse speaks of God in the third person; 11:11 returns to God's own voice.

decisions.choice: "{{gender:자녀|아들}}들"
decisions.reason: Korean has two wordings here, so the English gender span is kept.

records.literal_gloss: They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt, and like a dove from [the] land of Assyria; and I will cause them to dwell in their houses, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: They will come trembling like a bird from Egypt, \q and like a dove from the land of Assyria, \q and I will make them dwell in their houses, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt, \q like doves from the land of Assyria, \q and I will settle them in their homes, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: They will hurry back from Egypt, trembling like birds. \q They will come from Assyria like doves. \q I will let them live in their own homes again, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

es.L: Vendrán temblando como un ave desde Egipto, \q y como una paloma desde la tierra de Asiria, \q y los haré habitar en sus casas, declara {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.B: Vendrán temblando como aves desde Egipto, \q como palomas desde la tierra de Asiria, \q y los estableceré en sus casas, afirma {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.
es.R: Volverán deprisa de Egipto, temblando como pájaros. \q Vendrán de Asiria como palomas. \q Haré que vuelvan a vivir en sus propias casas, dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}.

fr.L: Ils viendront en tremblant comme un oiseau d’Égypte, \q et comme une colombe du pays d’Assyrie, \q et je les ferai habiter dans leurs maisons, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Ils accourront en tremblant comme des oiseaux d’Égypte, \q comme des colombes du pays d’Assyrie, \q et je les établirai dans leurs maisons, déclare {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Ils reviendront vite d’Égypte, tremblants comme des oiseaux. \q Ils viendront d’Assyrie comme des colombes. \q Je les ferai de nouveau habiter dans leurs propres maisons, dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.

sw.L: Watakuja wakitetemeka kama ndege kutoka Misri, \q na kama hua kutoka nchi ya Ashuru, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawakalisha katika nyumba zao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Watakuja wakitetemeka kama ndege kutoka Misri, \q kama njiwa kutoka nchi ya Ashuru, \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawaweka katika nyumba zao, asema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Watarudi haraka kutoka Misri, wakitetemeka kama ndege. \q Watakuja kutoka Ashuru kama njiwa. \q Nitawafanya waishi tena katika nyumba zao wenyewe, anasema {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.

vi.L: Họ sẽ run rẩy đến như chim từ Ai Cập, \q và như bồ câu từ đất A-si-ri, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho họ ở trong nhà mình, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.B: Họ sẽ run rẩy bay về như chim từ Ai Cập, \q như bồ câu từ đất A-si-ri, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ cho họ định cư trong nhà mình, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán vậy.
vi.R: Họ sẽ vội vã trở về từ Ai Cập, run rẩy như chim. \q Họ sẽ từ A-si-ri trở về như bồ câu. \q Ta sẽ cho họ lại được ở trong nhà riêng của mình, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán.

ko.L: 그들이 이집트에서 새처럼, \q 앗시리아 땅에서 비둘기처럼 떨며 올 것이다. \q 내가 그들을 그들의 집에서 살게 하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 선언이다.
ko.B: 그들은 이집트에서 새처럼, \q 앗시리아 땅에서 비둘기처럼 떨며 날아올 것이다. \q 내가 그들을 자기 집에서 살게 하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.
ko.R: 그들은 이집트에서 새처럼 떨며 서둘러 돌아올 것이다. \q 앗시리아에서 비둘기처럼 날아올 것이다. \q 나는 그들이 다시 자기 집에서 살게 하겠다. {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 말한다.

decisions.choice: like a bird ... like a dove from Egypt and Assyria: the foolish dove of 7:11 coming home
decisions.reason: In 7:11 Ephraim is "like a dove, silly and without sense", calling to Egypt and going to Assyria for help. The same two lands, and the same bird, return here. The people who flew to those powers will fly back from them.

decisions.choice: I will settle them in their houses: the exile undone
decisions.reason: The threat of verse 5 and of 9:3, that Ephraim would live in a foreign land, is reversed: God will bring them back to live in their own homes.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD: the end of the poem and of a section
decisions.reason: The formula closes the oracle, and the Hebrew text marks a section break after this verse. The next verse is 12:1 in the Hebrew text and 11:12 in many Bibles; see the note there.

decisions.choice: declares the LORD (L, B); says the LORD (R) ... live in their own homes again (R)
decisions.reason: The formula as set for the prophets. Readable adds "again" to show that this is a return (m2).
